transcript:
YOU
Use compareGeoDatasets with originalPath set to the 2025-04-08 GeoTIFF and modifiedPath set to the 2025-09-22 GeoTIFF. Summarize what differs between the two dates and what the comparison does not prove.
PAPYRUS
I'll inspect both rasters first so the comparison is grounded in actual metadata, then run the diff.
◫ Raster inspector ↗
◫ Raster inspector ↗
PAPYRUS
Both rasters are the same grid (728×680, EPSG:32610, identical bounds), so the diff is spatially valid. Running the comparison now.
◫ Raster Diff ↗
PAPYRUS
Raster Diff — Salinas NIR, 2025-04-08 vs 2025-09-22
Comparison basis (verified, not assumed): both files are single-band 8-bit GeoTIFFs on an identical grid — 728 × 680 px, EPSG:32610 (UTM zone 10N), bounds 660620–667900 E × 4065320–4072120 N. Because extent, CRS and raster size match exactly, pixel-for-pixel differencing is spatially meaningful; no resampling or reprojection was applied. All statistics below come from the sampled preview (2,160 pixels), not the full rasters.
What differs between the two dates
PROPERTY	2025-04-08 (ORIGINAL)	2025-09-22 (MODIFIED)
Sampled min	19	31
Sampled max	203	184
Sampled mean	104.71	99.25
Mean reflectance falls modestly: −5.46 DN (~−5% relative). The scene is slightly darker in September than in April.
Dynamic range compresses at both ends. The high tail drops hard (203 → 184), and the low tail rises (19 → 31). April has both the brightest and the darkest sampled pixels; September is a more homogeneous scene.
The change is not a uniform offset. Inspecting matched positions in the two previews, many pixels move by small amounts in both directions, and the largest support differences are positive (April higher than September), not a flat shift. That is consistent with a spatially varying scene change rather than a sensor gain change applied to the whole image.
Structure is retained. Field boundaries, block edges and the sharp high/low contrasts visible in the April array are still present in the September array at the same locations — the two dates are clearly the same site viewed twice, not two different scenes.
The diff is read-only: neither source file was written to, and no derived GeoTIFF was produced by this call.
What the comparison does not prove
It does not establish what caused the change. A drop in NIR radiance between April and September is equally consistent with crop growth and canopy closure, senescence or harvest, surface moisture change, different atmospheric/aerosol conditions, different sun–target–sensor geometry, or different acquisition dates within a growing season. The diff alone cannot separate these.
It is not a calibrated reflectance change. These are 8-bit DN arrays with no QA/cloud mask, no scaling factor and no stated band identity beyond the filename. Absolute or physically meaningful reflectance differences cannot be derived from them.
It does not prove the comparison covers the whole image. Only a spatially sampled subset (2,160 of 495,040 pixels, roughly 0.4%) was summarized. Localized change outside the sample is not ruled out, and the reported min/max/mean are not full-raster statistics.
It does not prove the pixels are co-registered. Grids match in dimensions, CRS and bounds, but identical framing does not guarantee identical footprint — differing acquisition geometry, terrain relief or reprojection error can leave residual sub-pixel misregistration that would inflate apparent per-pixel differences, especially at field edges.
It does not prove surface change of any specific kind. No classification, no NDVI/vegetation index, no thresholding and no trend analysis was performed. A "NIR went down" reading is a description of the numbers, not evidence of a particular land-cover transition.
It says nothing about the intervening period. Two endpoints cannot show whether the change was gradual, a step, or whether intermediate dates moved the other way.
It does not prove the two scenes are comparable acquisitions. Without per-scene metadata (cloud cover, tile ID, processing baseline, acquisition time), I cannot assert the two dates were captured under equivalent conditions.
To make this evidentiary rather than descriptive, you would need per-scene metadata and a cloud/QA mask, both dates from the same processing baseline, an explicit coregistration check, full-raster (not sampled) statistics, and a stated interpretation threshold — ideally with intermediate dates. I can run any of those next if you point me at the supporting metadata.
Done
ACTIVITY
